newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No trade in Prospur at S.Africa JSE debut.
newsitem.headline: No trade in Prospur at S.Africa JSE debut.

text.p: South Africa's Prospur Packaging and Plastics Ltd, the firm which listed on the Johannesburg bourse on Monday, had not seen a single trade by noon (100GMT) after its unbundling from Harwill Investments Ltd.
Dealers said that the lack of interest stemmed from Harwill's general inactivity and confusion following the "complex" transactions accompanying the listing.

"Harwill is not very active and to get shares in Prospur you had to be a shareholder in Harwill," one dealer said. "There's also been a bit of confusion about the various offers and it may take people a while to work it out," she added.

Sponsoring brokers Huysamer Stals said that shareholders in Harwill would receive 28.23 shares in Prospur for every 100 shares held in Harwill at an issue price of 100 cents. There was no public offer.
The subscription offer was expected to raise raise five million rand, before expenses, in Prospur and the sale offer to raise eight million rand in Harwill.

Harwill chairman Renier van Rooyen last week told Business Day newspaper that the listing would free Prospur, which consists of Harwill's three profitable plastic packaging divisions, of Harwill's past losses. Prospur would also look at expanding through acquisitions and organic growth.
Harwill posted a 97 percent slump in attributable earnings to 34,000 rand in the six months to December, the paper said. Harwill was last up 25 cents at 650 cents. It last traded on July 2.
Neither Prospur nor Harwill management could immediately be reached for comment.
